value.lineage: README: 'brief instructions to install, compile and run stringmol version 0.2.2' and 'url https://github.com/franticspider/stringmol.git' (a different GitHub owner than the pinned uoy-research repo). src/DEVNOTES.md: 'It begain in the Plazzmid project ... 2 years further work during EvoEvo'; flavours 'Vanilla' (papers before 2016), 'RUTSAC' (with Adam Nellis for the stringmol web app), 'Spatial' (with Paulien Hogeweg for R-P evolution, actively under development), 'FPGA' (Matthew Rowlings/Martin Trezfer, external), 'RStringmol' (external). Trial type 1 'ALife XII' is called 'the grand-daddy stringmol program'. CGI.md describes a web API (bind/step/bucket) from Adam Nellis. Headers on microbial_ga.* credit Verena Fischer. || main loop (reader, from the code): Each timestep (stringPM::TimestepIncrement) drains the 'now' agent list by picking molecules at random, applying decay at decayrate, and -- while energy remains -- either trying to bind an unbound molecule to a random unbound partner with probability from a Smith-Waterman alignment against the substitution matrix (setting one as active executor and one as passive), or executing the active molecule's current opcode on the pair (search, move, copy-with-mutation, increment, toggle, if-label, cleave which releases a product into the population, or terminate), each executed step costing one unit of energy, then moving the molecules to the 'next' list which becomes 'now' for the following step.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: An 'Automata Chemistry': simulate containers (well-mixed, or spatial grids) of string molecules that bind by sequence alignment and execute each other as micro-programs (copy, cleave, search, move, toggle, if) so that replicase strings reproduce with mutation, and study the resulting species/population dynamics.

organs.mechanism: an unbound string meets a partner with probability 1 - (1 - area ratio)^n; the pair aligns one string's complement against the other; l = the shorter matched span, bind probability 0 if l <= 2 else min(score, l - 1.124) / (l - 1.124) (commented 'BRUTAL HACK'); binding costs one energy unit; the later-matching string becomes the active one
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the cache list is passed by value, so its head update is lost when the list is empty; a second alignment is computed and discarded

organs.mechanism: opcodes search ($, deterministic best alignment of the complemented template), move, copy (=, with indel probability indelrate and substitution to an adjacent opcode at subrate), increment, toggle, if-label (success probability (score/len)^len), cleave and terminate; every executed op costs one energy unit
organs.output: a modified string, possibly a product
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: '}' falls through into default; a deletion advances the instruction pointer instead of the read pointer; a fixed 128-byte memset on a variable buffer

organs.mechanism: the string from the active flow pointer to the end becomes a new agent and the parent is truncated; zero-length parents are destroyed
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the agent counter is never advanced here (pointer incremented instead of count) and the next-list head is passed by value, so a product can be lost when that list is empty

organs.mechanism: each selected agent first decays with probability decayrate (default 1/65^2), freeing its partner; no reaction happens without energy; default mutation rates indel 3.06e-8, substitution 1e-5
